content:
> **Key answer**: This article will provide a sampling checklist for buyers, print engineers and suppliers to use together. Abrasion performance should be evaluated after transfer, handling, folding, packing and finishing, not only by looking at the freshly stamped surface. PINTE product information indicates that this wear-resistant series can achieve approximately 200 rub cycles under a 4 lb weighted test without obvious colour loss or obvious loss of the metallic layer. Final performance should still be confirmed on the actual substrate.

## Why does this question matter?

A foil that transfers successfully is not automatically a foil that will remain stable through packaging production and distribution. Paper boxes may be die-cut, folded, packed, transported, displayed and touched by end users. Soft-touch paper, soft-touch film and textured specialty paper can present different surface energy, coating structure and roughness from standard coated paper, so colour and gloss alone are not enough to judge compatibility.

A professional sourcing decision should answer three separate questions: can the foil transfer completely, can the stamped layer adhere to the substrate, and can the surface retain its colour and metallic appearance after the expected rubbing and finishing processes?

## PINTE wear-resistance test information

Abrasion performance should be evaluated after transfer, handling, folding, packing and finishing, not only by looking at the freshly stamped surface. PINTE product information indicates that this wear-resistant series can achieve approximately 200 rub cycles under a 4 lb weighted test without obvious colour loss or obvious loss of the metallic layer. Final performance should still be confirmed on the actual substrate.

The technical record for a production-relevant test should include the following:

## Suitable papers and surfaces

The foil is positioned for target paper, laminated paper, soft-touch paper, soft-touch film and specialty paper. Compatibility still needs to be confirmed by sampling because papers with the same commercial name can differ in coating, basis weight, surface energy, texture and lamination.

- **Soft-touch paper**: the tactile coating can improve the visual and sensory effect but may narrow the adhesion window. Check transfer completeness and edge condition after rubbing.

- **Soft-touch film**: surface treatment varies significantly by film supplier and finishing route. Test the actual film instead of using coated paper as a substitute.

- **Coated paper**: a relatively uniform surface can provide a useful baseline, but water-based coating, UV varnish and lamination must still be recorded.

- **Specialty paper**: texture, porosity and roughness can reduce contact in certain areas. Test solid areas, fine details and the actual artwork separately.

## Process variables that affect abrasion resistance

1. **Substrate surface**: coating, lamination, ink and residual additives can change adhesion.

1. **Stamping temperature**: too little heat may cause incomplete transfer; excessive heat can soften edges or damage the surface.

1. **Pressure and die condition**: uneven pressure can cause missing foil, while excessive pressure can deform the substrate.

1. **Machine speed and dwell time**: the available heat and contact time change with speed.

1. **Artwork structure**: solid areas, fine lines, small type and complex logos do not have the same risk profile.

1. **Post-processing**: lamination, varnishing, die-cutting, folding and assembly can alter the final rub result.

## How should sampling be organized?

Use the same paper, ink, surface treatment, die and machine conditions expected in production. Prepare at least three sample groups: one for visual inspection, one for rub testing and one retained as a control sample. Record the foil series, colour, substrate, temperature, pressure, speed and date on every sample.

For sampling communication, sample shipment and production approval, confirm the following before approval:

- whether the colour changes visibly after rubbing;

- whether the metallic layer flakes or peels;

- whether fine lines and small type remain complete;

- whether solid areas show pinholes or missing transfer;

- whether folding, die-cutting and assembly create delamination;

- whether different lots provide consistent results.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does a 4 lb rub test represent every packaging condition?

No. It is a result under a defined condition. Actual performance depends on the substrate, stamping window, finishing process and handling environment.

### Can abrasion-resistant foil guarantee zero flaking?

Avoid absolute claims. The correct approach is to define the actual substrate and acceptance method, then confirm the result through sampling.

### Why can production behave differently from the approved sample?

The paper lot, machine, die, pressure, speed or finishing route may change. Complete sampling records improve repeatability.

### What should a buyer request from a supplier?

Ask for the product specification, suitable substrates, test conditions, sample roll, recommended process window and lot traceability information.

## Conclusion and technical support

Foil selection should not rely only on colour, gloss or a general marketing statement. A more reliable process connects test data, target substrate, stamping conditions and post-processing in one sampling record. PINTE can support foil selection and sampling for target paper, laminated paper, soft-touch paper, soft-touch film and specialty paper based on the actual material and production requirements.

> **Evidence status**: The 4 lb and approximately 200-cycle claim is based on PINTE product information and should be verified by the technical team against the test report, sample images and final acceptance criteria before publication.
